analysis:
Both changed files are Swift test files only: NemotronSuperLocalHTTPReasoningToolTests.swift and NemotronSuperLocalHTTPTests.swift. No production code, auth, crypto, attestation, coordinator protocol or key handling changed.

ReasoningToolTests head lines 110-124 move the json_object response_format plus tools combination from the invalid-400 list to a supported path. The tests expect a tool call to be returned as a call, a JSON-only answer to pass, and a non-JSON answer to return 422. This implies a production behavior change in a Super local HTTP hook that is not in the supplied evidence. That hook is a loopback, bearer-token-gated local inference server (127.0.0.1) outside the coordinator-provider WebSocket boundary. It does not touch TB-002, TB-011 or the key and attestation assets (A-003, A-015, A-016). The 422 validation path and the streamed failure path, which leaks no held text, remain tested at lines 100-109.

NemotronSuperLocalHTTPTests patch (head lines 221-225, 251-252) removes the 8 MiB oversized-body refusal test case. The new comment says the upload limit answers 413 first. The existing test in the base at lines 148-155 already asserts localInferenceMaxUploadBytes+1 gives contentTooLarge before raw-hook selection, so the upload-size DoS control is still covered by a test. A residual gap is that the encoded-body bound inside the hook is now untested and described as unreachable. This is a coverage reduction, not a vulnerability.

Remaining questions for integration: the production change that enables tools plus response_format was not supplied. Confirm that it keeps the tool-call and JSON validation fail-closed, and that no held text leaks on error. No finding is raised because the source is not visible.
